newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Erste says plans Creditanstalt statement shortly.
newsitem.headline: Erste says plans Creditanstalt statement shortly.

text.p: Austrian savings bank Die Erste said it would most probably issue a statement later on Friday on its bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in sell-off candidate Creditanstalt.

Die Erste leads a consortium of bidders, including insurer EA-Generali AG, which has proposed to form a joint holding company with Creditanstalt. The deadline for a final bid set by Finance Minister Viktor Klima last week expires today.
"We have no comment right now, but we plan to issue a statement later today," a spokeswoman for Die Erste Oesterreichische Spar-Casse Bank AG told Reuters.

EA-Generali declined to say whether the group was ready to make its final offer. "We certainly are in the final phase," EA-Generali board member Guenter Neumann told Reuters, adding that he did not know whether a bid would be submitted on Friday or Monday.

Klima earlier this week said he still expected a firm offer for Austria's number two bank, which has been on the government's sell-off list for more than six years now, to land on his desk before the end of the week.
The consortium around Die Erste is the only known bidder for the state's stake in Creditanstalt, which investment bank JP Morgan last year valued at about 18 billion schillings.

However, Klima this week indicated alternative solutions could not be ruled out completely. Several international bidders over the past years have dropped out of the race for Creditanstalt, but the minister indicated some of the old contacts were still in place. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
